messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] csv problem: very basic, really unnerving...
parts:
I bet this is due to (single and/or double) quotes in the corpus files
or other (sometimes hidden) characters. I just had a similar case
where a concordance I was sent first looked fine but upon import with
read.table threw cells out of alignment. You need to make sure that
you read in with read.table and that quote and comment.char are set to
"" and that there are no other encoding issues; this is how this
always worked out for me.

Cheers,
STG
--

messages.subject: Recommendations for developing a datafile of R Digests
parts:
I was hoping for some advice regarding creating a data file(s) from R
Digests. I save these files into my mail program (Eudora) but they
are now in several folders because of the space they take up. To
speed up my mail program and to facilitate searches, I was planning
on using R to do searches. I know there are search engines on the
Cran site but often it can be difficult locating specific topics.

My question concerns the best format to save the digests in to allow
searching. I've used the TM package previously but only on csv files.
Am I better off creating one large text file, multiple text files in
a folder or several folders or some other method. I was planning to
strip the headers from the digests because these repeat subsequent content.

Any suggestions regarding the above or comments on issues, that I
should consider, are appreciated,

Regards

Bob

messages.author: d95dc06d463d4250
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Recommendations for developing a datafile of R Digests
parts: On Sat, Mar 24, 2012 at 11:42 PM, Bob Green <bgr...@dyson.brisnet.org.au> wrote:

I was hoping for some advice regarding creating a data file(s) from R Digests. I save these files into my mail program (Eudora) but they are now in several folders because of the space they take up. To speed up my mail program and to facilitate searches, I was planning on using R to do searches. I know there are search engines on the Cran site but often it can be difficult locating specific topics.

With other lists, which are much more prolific than this or R-users, I have kept archives in mbox format. When I need to search through the messages (in either text or RFC-x821/x822 headers) the grep utility comes in handy to locate the message(s) of interest. Depending upon my need the -A or -B options may be necessary to give the surrounding context. Or depending on the version of grep installed the --after-context and --before-context options respectively.

However, if I needed extended searches over email texts I would use one of the search systems available; either mg from the Witten/Moffat/Bell book "Managing Gigabytes" or Lucene from Apache. Both are freely available as source code. Lucene is available as pre-built binaries ready for the Java Virtual Machine. Lucene also has a richer search language. Whereas in the past I would have used mg today I'd be going for Lucene.

If my intent in putting messages archives into R so as to analyse the texts in some way, maybe using the tm module, I would seriously thinking about adding in a Lucene support module to R --- someone may already have done that anyway.
Any suggestions regarding the above or comments on issues, that I should consider, are appreciated,

You should clarify what it is that you want to search for and choose an appropriate tool: grep, mg or Lucene, or something else. Don't be beguiled by the fact that as your archives contain R mailing list messages you must then use R to process them. Use R only for what it is good for; use support tools for what they are good for; if necessary combine them together and assist us all by so doing.

Regards, Trevor.
